title: Miserere mei, Deus
hook: A psalm for the Sistine Chapel, with a high note that floats above everything.

painting.title: Pope Pius VII in the Sistine Chapel
painting.pairingNote: A papal service in the Sistine Chapel, with Michelangelo’s Last Judgment on the end wall: the room the Miserere was written for, where the Pope’s choir sang it in Holy Week for generations.

title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 3 in G major
hook: Three violins, three violas, three cellos and no soloist: everyone is the soloist in turn.

painting.title: The Little Concert (Il concertino)
painting.pairingNote: Three string players crowd round one table of music in a Venetian drawing room, two decades after Bach’s concerto for strings in groups of three.

title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 5 in D major
hook: The harpsichord, usually heard in the background, walks to the front and takes over.

painting.title: The Flute Concert of Frederick the Great at Sanssouci
painting.pairingNote: A flute, a violin and a harpsichord lead a Prussian court concert, with Bach’s son Carl Philipp Emanuel at the keyboard; the same three soloists Bach chose for this concerto.

title: Cello Suite No. 1 in G major
hook: One cello, alone, playing melody, bass and harmony at once, beginning with the best-known prelude ever written for it.

painting.title: Portrait of a Cello Player
painting.pairingNote: A working musician of Bach’s own generation, painted in Lombardy around 1740 with his hand on the neck of a Baroque cello, the instrument these suites were written for.

title: Keyboard Concerto No. 1 in D minor
hook: The whole band and the soloist start in stark octaves, and the drive in D minor hardly lets up.

painting.title: Dresden from the Right Bank of the Elbe below the Augustus Bridge
painting.pairingNote: The dome of the Frauenkirche, where Bach played the new Silbermann organ in 1736, rises over the city he visited as Saxon court composer; one theory links these concertos to his visit of 1738.

title: Orchestral Suite No. 3 in D major
hook: Trumpets, drums and French dances, and at the centre the Air, for strings alone.

painting.title: La Camargo Dancing
painting.pairingNote: The star dancer of the Paris Opéra around 1730, the years of this suite; the French style of dancing that Bach’s gavottes, bourrée and gigue imitate.

title: Partita No. 2 in D minor for solo violin
hook: Four short dances, then the Chaconne, a quarter of an hour for one violin built on a four-bar phrase.

painting.title: Vanitas Still Life with Self-Portrait
painting.pairingNote: A violin and its bow lie beside a skull, an overturned glass and an open pocket watch, a meditation on time and loss; some scholars hear the Chaconne as Bach’s own memorial.

title: Adagio for Strings
hook: One long, slowly climbing melody that became America’s music for mourning.

painting.title: The Home of the Heron
painting.pairingNote: Painted the year before Inness died, a lone heron by dark water under a fading, glowing sky; the same hush and slow-burning light as the Adagio.

title: Piano Concerto No. 3 in C minor
hook: A quiet drumbeat Beethoven planned in 1796 waits at the heart of his stormiest concerto.

painting.title: Landscape with Hammer Mill
painting.pairingNote: Painted in Vienna around 1800, while the concerto was taking shape; a forge glows in a dark valley, its hammer beating like the drum in the music, under a sky breaking into light.

title: Piano Concerto No. 5 in E-flat major, “Emperor”
hook: Written under French guns in 1809, it opens with the piano taking command.

painting.title: The Emperor Napoleon in His Study at the Tuileries
painting.pairingNote: The emperor whose army shelled Vienna while Beethoven was writing this concerto, painted in 1812, the year it was first heard there; the nickname “Emperor” was never Beethoven’s.

title: Piano Sonata No. 14 in C-sharp minor, “Moonlight”
hook: A hushed, slow ripple that everyone knows, then a short dance and a storm few expect.

painting.title: Two Men Contemplating the Moon
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: Two figures stand still under bare branches and watch the moon; it was in the 1820s, the decade Friedrich painted this, that a critic first heard moonlight in the sonata’s slow opening.

title: Piano Sonata No. 21 in C major, “Waldstein”
hook: A sonata that starts with a quiet pulse and ends in a blaze of light, often heard as a sunrise.

painting.title: Sun Rising through Vapour
painting.pairingNote: Painted within three years of the sonata, a pale sun breaking through morning mist over a glassy sea; in Italy the sonata is known as “L’Aurora”, the dawn, for the way the finale’s theme glows out of the haze of the pedal.

title: Piano Sonata No. 23 in F minor, “Appassionata”
hook: Whispered threats, sudden eruptions and a finale that never stops running.

painting.title: An Eruption of Vesuvius
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: A volcano bursts into fire above a dark, still bay; the sonata works the same way, long stretches of tense quiet broken by sudden explosions.

title: Piano Sonata No. 8 in C minor, “Pathétique”
hook: Heavy chords, a fast storm, and one of Beethoven’s best-loved slow tunes.

painting.title: The Death of Socrates
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: A man meets death calmly, one hand raised, while his friends collapse in grief around him; the grave, noble pathos of the late 18th century that the sonata’s title names.

title: Piano Trio in B-flat major, “Archduke”
hook: Beethoven’s broadest trio, and the piece he played at his last public concert as a pianist.

painting.title: Caspar David Friedrich in His Studio
painting.pairingNote: Painted in 1811, the year Beethoven finished the trio; an artist alone in a bare, quiet room, wholly absorbed in his work, with the same unhurried calm as the trio’s opening theme and its hymn-like slow movement.

title: String Quartet No. 15 in A minor
hook: Written after a serious illness, with a slow hymn of thanks at its centre.

painting.title: Salisbury Cathedral from the Bishop’s Garden
painting.pairingNote: An old Gothic cathedral stands in washed, clearing light, painted the year after the quartet; in his hymn of thanks Beethoven also turned to something old, an ancient church scale, and made it sound new.

title: Symphony No. 3 in E-flat major, “Eroica”
hook: The symphony Beethoven wrote for Napoleon, and then tore his name from.

painting.title: Bonaparte at the Pont d’Arcole
painting.pairingNote: Gros’s study for his portrait of the young general Bonaparte, flag in hand, painted in Milan in 1796; the hero Beethoven admired before Napoleon crowned himself emperor.

title: Symphony No. 5 in C minor
hook: Four notes, and everything that can be built from them.

painting.title: Snow Storm: Hannibal and his Army Crossing the Alps
painting.pairingNote: A struggle through darkness with light breaking at the edge of the storm, painted within four years of the symphony.

title: Symphony No. 6 in F major, “Pastoral”
hook: A day in the country, from the first breath of air to the thanksgiving after a storm.

painting.title: Heroic Landscape with Rainbow
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: A herdsman pipes to his goats while the clouds part and a rainbow spans the valley; an Austrian contemporary of Beethoven paints the calm after the storm.

title: Symphony No. 7 in A major
hook: Four movements, each driven by a single rhythm; Wagner called it the apotheosis of the dance.

painting.title: The Peasant Dance
painting.pairingNote: Villagers stamp and spin to the drone of a bagpipe; Wagner called the Seventh “the apotheosis of the dance”, and its trio has a drone of its own.

title: Symphony No. 9 in D minor, “Choral”
hook: The symphony that found it needed the human voice.

painting.title: Morning (first version), also called The Small Morning
painting.pairingNote: A radiant vision of light and new beginning from Beethoven’s own generation, matching the finale’s hymn to joy.

title: Violin Concerto in D major
hook: It begins with five soft drumbeats, and the violin sings rather than shows off.

painting.title: Marie Joséphine Charlotte du Val d’Ognes (Young Woman Drawing)
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: A young woman drawing by a bright window in Paris in 1801; stillness, concentration and clear light, like the violin’s long singing line.

title: Violin Sonata No. 9 in A major, “Kreutzer”
hook: A violin sonata written like a concerto, for a duel between two equal players.

painting.title: Ludwig van Beethoven with a Lyre-Guitar
painting.pairingNote: Beethoven as he looked in 1804–05, a year after he first played the sonata with George Bridgetower.

title: Symphonie fantastique
hook: An obsession told in five scenes, ending at a witches’ sabbath.

painting.title: Witches’ Sabbath, or the Great He-Goat
painting.pairingNote: Painted within a decade of the symphony, the same nightmare gathering that Berlioz stages in his finale.
painting.medium: Oil on mural, transferred to canvas

title: String Quartet No. 2 in D major
hook: A chemist’s love letter to his wife, with one of the most famous nocturnes ever written.

painting.title: Moonlit Night
painting.pairingNote: A young woman alone on a bench in a moonlit garden, painted a year before the quartet; a nocturne in paint, for a quartet its composer gave to his wife.

title: Clarinet Quintet in B minor
hook: Brahms meant to stop composing, then heard a clarinettist and wrote this autumnal farewell.

painting.title: Interior with Young Woman Seen from the Back
painting.pairingNote: A woman turned away in a grey, silent room, painted a decade after the quintet; the same hushed, inward mood as Brahms’s late chamber music.

title: Piano Concerto No. 2 in B-flat major
hook: Brahms called it “a very small piano concerto”; it has four movements and lasts almost an hour.

painting.title: March Mood: Early Spring in the Vienna Woods
painting.pairingNote: Early spring in the Vienna Woods, where Brahms finished the concerto at Pressbaum in 1881, painted three years later.

title: Symphony No. 1 in C minor
hook: Years in the making, it climbs from pounding drums in the dark to a horn call over the mountains.

painting.title: The Lake of Thun
painting.pairingNote: A sunlit Swiss mountain lake under snowy peaks; the world of the alphorn call Brahms sent to Clara Schumann in 1868 and set at the heart of the finale.

title: Symphony No. 2 in D major
hook: A sunlit symphony from one summer by an Austrian lake, with shadows Brahms put there on purpose.

painting.title: View of the Wörthersee with Maria Loretto and Freyenthurn Castle
painting.pairingNote: The Carinthian lake where Brahms spent the summer of 1877 writing this symphony, painted by a local landscape painter a generation earlier.

title: Symphony No. 4 in E minor
hook: An autumn symphony that ends in tragedy, built on a tune borrowed from Bach.

painting.title: Isle of the Dead (third version)
painting.pairingNote: Painted two years before the symphony, with the same grave stillness and the same refusal of a consoling ending.

title: Violin Concerto in D major
hook: Written for a great violinist friend, with a stormy entrance, an oboe’s song and a Hungarian dance to finish.

painting.title: Picnic in May
painting.pairingNote: A sunlit picnic on a Hungarian hillside, painted a few years before the concerto, with the same open-air warmth and the Hungarian accent of its finale.

title: Violin Concerto No. 1 in G minor
hook: A prelude, a great slow song and a dance; the concerto that eclipsed everything else its composer wrote.

painting.title: Iphigenia
painting.pairingNote: Painted by a German Romantic a few years before the concerto, a woman gazing out to sea in silent longing; the same long, singing line as Bruch’s Adagio.

title: Symphony No. 4 in E-flat major, “Romantic”
hook: A horn call at daybreak, a hunt in the forest, and a nickname Bruckner chose himself.

painting.title: Medieval City on a River
painting.pairingNote: A Gothic cathedral, a castle on the hill and a procession of riders below, the dream of the Middle Ages that Bruckner’s own programme for the symphony describes, with a city at daybreak and knights riding out.

title: Symphony No. 7 in E major
hook: A melody Bruckner said came to him in a dream, and a funeral hymn for Wagner.

painting.title: Three Women in Church
painting.pairingNote: Painted in the same years and shown in Vienna in 1882 while Bruckner was writing the symphony there, three village women at prayer, the plain country faith Bruckner grew up in.

title: Piano Concerto No. 1 in E minor
hook: A twenty-year-old’s farewell to Warsaw, with a slow movement he called a moonlit reverie.

painting.title: View of Morysinek
painting.pairingNote: Still water, a white villa and a rainbow after rain in a park on the edge of Warsaw, painted a few years after Chopin left the city for good; the gentle Polish light of the Romance.

title: Piano Concerto No. 2 in F minor
hook: Chopin’s first concerto, with a slow movement inspired by a young singer he loved in silence.

painting.title: View of the Kazimierz Palace from Powiśle
painting.pairingNote: The Warsaw University palace above the Vistula, where Chopin went to school and beside which he grew up; painted in the decade after he wrote this concerto and left the city for good.

title: Piano Sonata No. 2 in B-flat minor
hook: The sonata with the funeral march, and a finale like wind over the graves.

painting.title: A Burial at Ornans
painting.pairingNote: Villagers in black gather round an open grave, painted in the months around Chopin’s own funeral in Paris in October 1849, when his funeral march was played at the graveside.

title: La mer
hook: The sea in three sketches, painted with an orchestra instead of a brush.

painting.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (The Great Wave)
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: Debussy kept a print of this wave in his study and asked for it on the cover of the first edition of La mer in 1905.
painting.medium: Woodblock print; ink and color on paper

title: Prélude à l’après-midi d’un faune
hook: Ten minutes of a hot afternoon, a flute, and the start of modern music.

painting.title: A Morning. The Dance of the Nymphs
painting.pairingNote: Nymphs dancing in a hazy, softly lit glade: the dreamlike world of Mallarmé’s faun, who is never sure whether the nymphs were real.

title: Cello Concerto in B minor
hook: Written by a homesick Dvořák in New York, for an instrument he had long thought unfit for a concerto.

painting.title: Birch Mood
painting.pairingNote: An autumn birch wood in Bohemia, painted two years after the concerto; the Czech countryside Dvořák longed for in New York and went home to in 1895.

title: Piano Quintet No. 2 in A major
hook: Five players, two Slavic dances and a lament that keeps breaking into joy.

painting.title: Company in the Country
painting.pairingNote: A Czech painter’s summer outing by a stream, friends lounging and girls wading in the water, two years after Dvořák wrote this sunny quintet in the country at Vysoká.

title: String Quartet No. 12 in F major, “American”
hook: Written in about two weeks during a happy summer in a Czech village in Iowa.

painting.title: Canal Scene
painting.collection: Terra Foundation for American Art, Chicago
painting.pairingNote: A sunny canal lock in the American countryside, painted in 1893, the summer Dvořák spent in Iowa; plain colours and open air, like the quartet.

title: Symphony No. 8 in G major
hook: A summer in the Bohemian countryside, with birdsong, a village band and trumpets that call to the dance.

painting.title: The Chrudimka Valley
painting.pairingNote: A Bohemian valley in high summer, meadow, haystack and woods, painted two years before Dvořák wrote this symphony in the Bohemian countryside.

title: Symphony No. 9 in E minor, “From the New World”
hook: A Czech composer’s postcard from America, written with homesickness in the ink.

painting.title: Among the Sierra Nevada, California
painting.collection: Smithsonian American Art Museum, Washington, D.C.
painting.pairingNote: The vast, luminous American landscape as a European-trained artist imagined it, which is exactly what Dvořák did in sound.

title: Cello Concerto in E minor
hook: Elgar’s last major work, written in the year after the First World War; quiet, autumnal and deeply private.

painting.title: We Are Making a New World
painting.pairingNote: A pale sun over a shattered wood on the Western Front, painted the year before the concerto; Elgar’s music, written in the months after the war, mourns a lost world in a much quieter voice.

title: Violin Concerto in B minor
hook: A concerto with a riddle at its heart, “Herein is enshrined the soul of .....”.

painting.title: Sisters
painting.pairingNote: Millais’s three eldest daughters; the youngest, on the right, is Alice, later Alice Stuart-Wortley, the friend Elgar called “Windflower” and whose name is often read into the concerto’s riddle.

title: Violin Sonata in A major
hook: A wedding present in which one gentle tune keeps returning, each time in a new guise.

painting.title: Listening to Schumann
painting.collection: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, Brussels
painting.pairingNote: Painted in Brussels three years before the sonata was first played in public there, it shows a woman lost in music, her face hidden in her hand.

title: Peer Gynt Suite No. 1
hook: A sunrise, a deathbed, a seductive dance and a hall full of trolls, four scenes from Ibsen’s play about a Norwegian dreamer.

painting.title: Soria Moria Palace
painting.pairingNote: The fairy-tale palace of Soria Moria glowing at sunrise above the mist, by the painter of Norway’s trolls; in the play, Peer comforts his dying mother with an imaginary sleigh ride to this very castle.

title: Piano Concerto in A minor
hook: A drum roll, a crash down the keyboard, and Norway arrives in the concert hall.

painting.title: Bridal Procession on the Hardangerfjord
painting.pairingNote: Norway’s best-loved picture of its own fjords and folk life, painted twenty years before the concerto; the same national romance that Grieg’s dances carry into the concert hall.

title: Cello Concerto No. 1 in C major
hook: Written for a friend in Haydn’s orchestra, lost for two centuries, found in Prague in 1961.

painting.title: The Gore Family with George, third Earl Cowper
painting.collection: Yale Center for British Art, New Haven
painting.pairingNote: A family making music around 1775, the father at the cello and his daughter at the keyboard; a decade earlier Haydn had written this concerto for the cellist of his prince’s orchestra.

title: String Quartet in C major, Op. 76 No. 3, “Emperor”
hook: Haydn’s hymn for the emperor, passed from one player to the next.

painting.title: Laxenburg from the Münkendorf Pavilion, looking south-west
painting.pairingNote: Painted for the imperial palace at Laxenburg, near Vienna, it shows a court hunting party crossing a wide, calm plain, the Habsburg world for which Haydn wrote his hymn to the emperor.

title: Symphony No. 104 in D major, “London”
hook: Haydn’s last symphony, written for London, opens in darkness and ends with a dance over a bagpipe drone.

painting.title: Westminster Bridge, with the Lord Mayor’s Procession on the Thames
painting.collection: Yale Center for British Art, New Haven
painting.pairingNote: London’s river on Lord Mayor’s Day, crowded with ceremonial barges; the rich, music-loving city that, half a century later, paid Haydn handsomely for his last symphony.

title: Symphony No. 94 in G major, “Surprise”
hook: A quiet tune, a little quieter, then a crash: Haydn’s most famous joke.

painting.title: Vauxhall Gardens
painting.collection: Yale Center for British Art, New Haven
painting.pairingNote: London’s concert-going crowd at an evening concert in the 1780s, busier looking at one another than at the orchestra: the public Haydn set out to catch off guard.
painting.medium: Watercolour, pen and black and grey ink, and graphite on laid paper

title: Trumpet Concerto in E-flat major
hook: Written for a new kind of trumpet that could play every note, and full of the tunes the old one never could.

painting.artist: Jan Brueghel the Elder and Peter Paul Rubens
painting.title: Hearing
painting.pairingNote: A room crowded with instruments, natural trumpets and horns among them: the valveless trumpet of a few notes that Weidinger’s keyed trumpet, and Haydn’s concerto, set free.

title: Piano Concerto No. 1 in E-flat major
hook: Under twenty minutes of fireworks, four movements without a break, and a triangle that scandalised a critic.

painting.title: Liszt at the Piano
painting.collection: Alte Nationalgalerie, Staatliche Museen zu Berlin
painting.pairingNote: Liszt at 29, the most famous pianist in Europe, playing to a circle of writers and musicians in Paris; the years when he was working on this concerto.

title: Piano Sonata in B minor
hook: Four movements folded into one, built from a handful of notes that keep changing shape.

painting.title: Christ Asleep during the Tempest
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: Painted in the same year Liszt finished the sonata, a storm with one still figure at its centre; the sonata, too, rages and then ends in quiet.

title: Symphony No. 1 in D major
hook: Mahler’s first symphony begins with nature waking at dawn and ends in a storm that breaks into triumph.

painting.title: Spring in the Prater
painting.pairingNote: Vienna’s Prater park at the very start of spring, the trees still bare and the light new, painted in the city where Mahler studied; for this symphony’s first movement he once used the title “Spring and no end”.

title: Symphony No. 2 in C minor, “Resurrection”
hook: It opens at a funeral and ends with a choir singing of rising again.

painting.title: The Resurrection (Isenheim Altarpiece)
painting.pairingNote: Christ rises in a blaze of light while the guards tumble, the moment the finale sings about. The 1963 American LP of this very recording carried a detail of the same altarpiece.

title: Symphony No. 3 in D minor
hook: A whole summer in six movements, from sleeping rock to flowers, animals, angels and love.

painting.title: Spring in the Alps
painting.collection: J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles
painting.pairingNote: Painted the year after Mahler finished the symphony, it is a hymn to nature waking after winter, with mountains, meadows, animals and people in one picture, which is the Third’s own plan.

title: Symphony No. 4 in G major
hook: Sleigh bells, a fiddling Death and a child’s song of heaven, in Mahler’s gentlest symphony.

painting.title: Self-Portrait with Death Playing the Fiddle
painting.pairingNote: Death leans over the painter’s shoulder and plays a one-string fiddle; Alma Mahler said this picture inspired the symphony’s second movement, where a retuned violin plays Death’s dance.

title: Symphony No. 5
hook: From a funeral march to a love song to laughter.

painting.title: Death and Life
painting.pairingNote: Mahler’s Vienna in paint, and the symphony’s own journey in one image, from the figure of death to an embrace.

title: Symphony No. 9
hook: Mahler’s last finished symphony ends with music that slowly dies away into silence.

painting.title: Small Tree in Late Autumn
painting.pairingNote: Painted in 1911, the year Mahler died and a year before this symphony was first heard in Vienna, a bare young tree holding on alone against an empty sky.

title: Octet in E-flat major
hook: Eight string players and a sixteen-year-old composer at full speed.

painting.title: The Friedrichsgracht, Berlin
painting.pairingNote: Rooftops and a canal in the heart of Berlin under a bright sky, painted by a Berlin artist in the decade after the Octet, which the sixteen-year-old Mendelssohn wrote in the same city.
painting.medium: Oil on paper, mounted on paper-fibre based board

title: Symphony No. 4 in A major, “Italian”
hook: A young traveller’s Italy in four movements, from sunlit opening to a whirling Roman dance.

painting.title: The Arrival of the Harvesters in the Pontine Marshes
painting.pairingNote: Harvesters arriving with an ox cart under a clear sky south of Rome, painted in the year Mendelssohn reached Italy; the same bright, festive Italy that the symphony’s outer movements celebrate.

title: Violin Concerto in E minor
hook: The violin sings from the second bar, and the three movements run on without a pause.

painting.title: The Balcony Room
painting.pairingNote: A breeze lifts a thin curtain and sunlight pours into an empty room in Berlin, Mendelssohn’s home city, painted the year the concerto was first played; the music has the same lightness and fresh air.

title: Ave verum corpus
hook: Forty-six bars for a small-town church choir, written less than six months before Mozart died.

painting.title: The Last Supper
painting.pairingNote: Christ holds up the bread of the Eucharist, the “true body” that the hymn greets in its first words.

title: Clarinet Concerto in A major
hook: Mozart’s last concerto, written for a friend’s clarinet weeks before he died.

painting.title: Italian Landscape with Mountains and a River
painting.collection: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston (Sarah Campbell Blaffer Foundation)
painting.pairingNote: Painted in the same years from Wright’s memories of Italy, it has the concerto’s warm, late light and its unhurried calm, with a shadow at the edges.

title: Serenade No. 13 in G major, “Eine kleine Nachtmusik”
hook: Mozart’s most famous serenade, finished in the summer he was writing Don Giovanni.

painting.title: Mezzetin
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: A comedian of the Italian theatre sings to his guitar in a garden; a serenade, the evening music that Mozart’s title, “a little night music”, names.

title: Concerto for Flute and Harp in C major
hook: Salon music for a duke who played the flute and his daughter, the harpist, written in Paris and never paid for.

painting.title: English Tea in the Salon des Quatre-Glaces at the Palais du Temple
painting.pairingNote: A Paris salon making music over tea, with the child Mozart at the keyboard: the aristocratic world the concerto was written for twelve years later.

title: Piano Concerto No. 20 in D minor
hook: Mozart’s first piano concerto in a minor key, dark and stormy, and the one Beethoven kept playing.

painting.title: The Nightmare
painting.pairingNote: Painted in 1781, the year Mozart settled in Vienna: the dark, uncanny taste of the age, which Mozart’s first minor-key piano concerto brought into the concert hall.

title: Piano Concerto No. 21 in C major
hook: A quiet march that grows into a festival, and one of the most famous slow movements Mozart wrote.

painting.title: The Swing
painting.pairingNote: A young woman flies up on a swing in a sunlit garden; the lightness and play of the concerto’s outer movements, and the dream of its Andante.

title: Piano Concerto No. 23 in A major
hook: A sunny concerto with one deeply sad slow movement at its heart.

painting.title: Mr and Mrs William Hallett (‘The Morning Walk’)
painting.pairingNote: Painted in 1785 and paid for on 4 March 1786, two days after Mozart finished the concerto, it shares the music’s light, feathery elegance and the shade at its edges.

title: Piano Sonata No. 11 in A major
hook: A gentle tune in six disguises, a graceful minuet, and the “Turkish” finale everyone can hum.

painting.title: Cornelis Calkoen on his Way to his Audience with Sultan Ahmed III
painting.pairingNote: Janissaries, the Ottoman sultan’s elite soldiers, throw themselves at dishes of rice in a courtyard of the Topkapı Palace; the military bands of these same soldiers were what Vienna’s “Turkish” fashion, and Mozart’s finale, set out to imitate.

title: Sinfonia concertante in E-flat major for violin and viola
hook: A conversation between two soloists, violin and viola, written in Salzburg after a journey that went wrong.

painting.title: The Mozart Family
painting.pairingNote: Painted in Salzburg in 1780–81, the year after the Sinfonia concertante; Leopold holds his violin, and on the wall hangs the portrait of Mozart’s mother, who had died in Paris during that journey.

title: Symphony No. 40 in G minor
hook: Classical elegance with a racing pulse underneath.

painting.title: A Shipwreck in Stormy Seas
painting.pairingNote: The same years, the same taste for storm and agitation held inside a perfectly balanced frame.

title: Symphony No. 41 in C major, “Jupiter”
hook: Mozart’s last symphony, ending in a finale where five tunes play at once.

painting.title: The Obelisk
painting.pairingNote: Painted a year before the symphony, it builds a vast, ordered space out of the columns and vaults of ancient Rome, with the same grandeur and the same calm Classical balance.

title: Canon and Gigue in D major
hook: Eight bass notes, played twenty-eight times, with one of the best-known tunes in the world above them.

painting.title: The Concert
painting.pairingNote: A woman with a bowed bass instrument and another at the harpsichord, in a Dutch room of the 1670s; the same two instruments that play the canon’s endless bass.

title: Symphony No. 1 in D major, “Classical”
hook: Haydn as he might have written in 1917, composed in a summer of revolution.

painting.title: Lady in Blue
painting.pairingNote: A modern Petersburg painter poses his sitter in an old-fashioned gown, with strollers in period dress in the park behind her; an older elegance seen through modern eyes, as in the symphony.

title: Piano Concerto No. 2 in C minor
hook: The concerto that brought Rachmaninoff back after three silent years.

painting.title: Red Sunset
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: A red evening light breaking over a dark river, painted a few years after the concerto; the same turn from gloom to glow that the music makes.

title: Piano Concerto No. 3 in D minor
hook: It begins with a melody that, Rachmaninoff said, wrote itself, and grows into one of the hardest concertos ever written.

painting.title: Blue Morning
painting.pairingNote: New York in 1909, painted by a young American realist in the year Rachmaninoff crossed the Atlantic to give this concerto its first performance there.

title: Boléro
hook: One rhythm, two tunes and fifteen minutes of crescendo. Then the floor gives way.

painting.title: El Jaleo
painting.pairingNote: A dancer in a Spanish tavern, lit from below and egged on by guitars and clapping hands, the scene Boléro was first staged in.

title: Piano Concerto in G major
hook: A whip crack, a Basque tune, a touch of jazz, and a slow melody that Ravel said nearly killed him.

painting.title: Basque Celebration (Dance at El Antiguo, San Sebastián)
painting.collection: Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya, Barcelona
painting.pairingNote: Women dance on a grassy headland above San Sebastián bay while a pipe and drum play, on the Basque coast just across the border from Ravel’s birthplace; the concerto’s opening tune has a Basque lilt.

title: String Quartet in F major
hook: Written at 28, dedicated to Fauré, and modelled on Debussy, yet unmistakably Ravel’s own.

painting.title: The Evening Air
painting.pairingNote: A calm, classical scene of figures under pines at dusk, built from small separate touches of pure colour; like Ravel’s quartet, an old, orderly form seen in new light.

title: Scheherazade
hook: A storyteller saves her life one tale at a time. Her voice is a solo violin.

painting.title: The Ninth Wave
painting.pairingNote: Survivors cling to the mast of a wrecked ship as the sea calms at sunrise, the shipwreck and stillness of Scheherazade’s last pages, painted by Russia’s great painter of the sea.

title: Cello Concerto No. 1 in A minor
hook: A whole concerto in under twenty minutes, without a pause, starting with a single chord.

painting.title: Impression, Sunrise
painting.pairingNote: Painted at Le Havre around November 1872, the month Saint-Saëns finished his concerto; a morning sun breaking through the mist, set down quickly and in one sweep.

title: Symphony No. 3 in C minor, “Organ”
hook: Saint-Saëns said he gave this symphony everything he had; the organ waits almost ten minutes for its first note.

painting.title: The Organ Rehearsal
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: Painted in Paris the year before the symphony, a singer rehearsing beside the organ in a church loft; Saint-Saëns had spent more than twenty years as an organist in Paris churches.

title: Piano Quintet in A major, “Trout”
hook: A summer holiday in five movements, with a song about a trout at its heart.

painting.title: The Angler
painting.pairingNote: An angler jerks a small fish out of a woodland brook while two young women look on; the scene of Schubert’s trout song, painted in the same gentle, small-town spirit.

title: Piano Sonata No. 21 in B-flat major
hook: Schubert’s last sonata, finished eight weeks before he died, with a low trill that haunts its calm.

painting.title: View of Dresden by Moonlight
painting.pairingNote: A quiet river city under the moon, painted by a contemporary of Schubert; the sonata’s calm, nocturnal glow and its long silences.

title: String Quartet No. 14 in D minor, “Death and the Maiden”
hook: Four players and one shadow, in a quartet built around Schubert’s song of Death coming for a young girl.

painting.title: Death and the Maiden
painting.pairingNote: Painted in Vienna under the same title, a girl clinging to a dark-robed figure of Death on a rumpled sheet, with the same mix of dread and tenderness as Schubert’s song.

title: String Quintet in C major
hook: Schubert’s last chamber work, finished two months before he died and never heard in his lifetime.

painting.title: The Stages of Life
painting.pairingNote: Five figures on an evening shore and five ships coming in, painted in Friedrich’s last working years; like the quintet, a late work in which calm and farewell sit side by side.

title: Symphony No. 5 in B-flat major
hook: A sunny symphony by a nineteen-year-old in love with Mozart, written for friends to play at home.

painting.title: The Hülsenbeck Children
painting.pairingNote: Three children racing through a sunlit garden: the youthful, open-air brightness of a nineteen-year-old’s symphony.

title: Symphony No. 8 in B minor, “Unfinished”
hook: Two movements, and nothing missing.

painting.title: The Abbey in the Oakwood
painting.pairingNote: A ruin that is more moving for being incomplete, in the hushed, wintry mood of the symphony’s opening.

title: Symphony No. 9 in C major, “The Great”
hook: Shelved as too long in Schubert’s lifetime, it was rescued by Schumann, who loved its “heavenly length”.

painting.title: View of the Dachstein with the Hallstätter See from the Hütteneckalm near Ischl
painting.pairingNote: The lakes and peaks of Upper Austria, where Schubert spent the summer of 1825 working on the symphony, painted by a Viennese contemporary on the same broad, sunlit scale.

title: Piano Concerto in A minor
hook: A love song for piano and orchestra, written for Clara Schumann to play.

painting.title: Barge Trip on the Elbe near Dresden
painting.pairingNote: A woman in a straw hat crosses the Elbe towards Dresden in clear morning light, painted by a Dresden doctor-artist; Schumann finished the concerto in Dresden, and later lived in Düsseldorf, where the picture now hangs.

title: Piano Quintet in E-flat major
hook: Written for Clara in a few weeks, the work that made piano and string quartet a team.

painting.title: A Symphony
painting.pairingNote: Piano, strings and voices making music together in a Romantic drawing room: the world of music at home that Schumann’s quintet brought into the concert hall.

title: Symphony No. 3 in E-flat major, “Rhenish”
hook: Schumann’s new life on the Rhine, with a solemn visit to Cologne Cathedral at its heart.

painting.title: Ideal View of Cologne Cathedral from the South-West
painting.pairingNote: The cathedral as it was meant to look when finished, painted while it still stood half-built; Schumann saw the unfinished building in 1850, and its memory runs through the solemn fourth movement.

title: Piano Concerto No. 2 in F major
hook: A birthday present from father to son, with a joke about piano practice in the finale.

painting.title: Two Young Girls at the Piano
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: Two girls practising at the piano at home: the everyday scales and exercises that Shostakovich, writing for his son Maxim, turned into a game.

title: String Quartet No. 8 in C minor
hook: A composer’s portrait of himself, written in three days, signed with his own initials in notes.

painting.title: The Ruins of the Old Kreuzkirche in Dresden
painting.pairingNote: Dresden’s great church lies in ruins after a bombardment in 1760; exactly two hundred years later Shostakovich wrote this quartet near the city, among the ruins of another war.

title: Symphony No. 5 in D minor
hook: A triumphant ending, or the sound of being forced to cheer? You decide.

painting.title: Barge Haulers on the Volga
painting.pairingNote: Men harnessed to a barge, straining under a load they did not choose; Russian endurance under pressure, painted sixty years before the symphony.

title: Symphony No. 2 in D major
hook: Begun in an Italian winter, heard in Finland as a song of freedom.

painting.title: Study from Koli
painting.pairingNote: Rocks, pines and Lake Pielisjärvi seen from the Koli heights, painted by Sibelius’s brother-in-law: the Finnish landscape that Finns have long heard in this symphony.

title: Symphony No. 5 in E-flat major
hook: A symphony that grows from a soft horn call into a hymn inspired by sixteen swans in flight.

painting.title: Mute Swans in Evening Flight
painting.pairingNote: Swans flying low over a northern marsh at dusk, painted by Sibelius’s Swedish contemporary; the finale was inspired by sixteen swans Sibelius watched in flight.

title: Violin Concerto in D minor
hook: The only concerto by a composer who had once dreamed of becoming a violin virtuoso himself.

painting.title: Lake Keitele
painting.pairingNote: A Finnish lake painted in 1905, the year the revised concerto was first played, by Sibelius’s friend Gallen-Kallela; long streaks of wind cut across the still surface as the violin’s line cuts across the soft strings.

title: Vltava (The Moldau), from Má vlast
hook: A river’s whole journey, from two forest springs to the city of Prague, in twelve minutes.

painting.title: Backwater of the Vltava at Roztoky
painting.pairingNote: A quiet bend of the Vltava just north of Prague, painted three years after Má vlast was first played complete; the river of the music, seen by a Czech painter of Smetana’s Prague.

title: Spem in alium
hook: Forty singers, forty separate parts, and one prayer that travels around the room.

painting.title: Paradise
painting.pairingNote: Tintoretto fills heaven with ring upon ring of saints and angels around one point of light, as Tallis gathers forty separate voices around a single prayer.

title: Piano Concerto No. 1 in B-flat minor
hook: The concerto its first listener tore apart, with an opening tune that never comes back.

painting.title: The Rooks Have Returned
painting.pairingNote: Painted by a Moscow teacher a few years before the concerto, the first thaw of a Russian spring; the finale is built on a Ukrainian song that calls the spring in.

title: Serenade for Strings in C major
hook: A bow to Mozart, a waltz and two Russian folk songs, for strings alone.

painting.title: Moscow Courtyard
painting.pairingNote: A sunlit Moscow courtyard with a church beyond, painted two years before the Serenade; ordinary Russian life in warm, clear light, like the waltz and the folk songs of the finale.

title: Symphony No. 4 in F minor
hook: A brass fanfare that Tchaikovsky called Fate, and a symphony that keeps running into it.

painting.title: Shrovetide
painting.pairingNote: Sledges, swings and crowds at a Russian winter fair; the “festive merriment of ordinary people” that Tchaikovsky said his finale pictures.

title: Symphony No. 5 in E minor
hook: One gloomy tune walks through all four movements and comes out the other side as a march.

painting.title: Morning in a Pine Forest
painting.pairingNote: Painted the year after the symphony, a dark Russian forest slowly filling with morning light; the same road from gloom to brightness that the motto theme travels.

title: Symphony No. 6 in B minor, “Pathétique”
hook: A symphony that ends not in triumph but in silence.

painting.title: Above Eternal Peace
painting.pairingNote: Painted a year after the symphony, a vast Russian landscape of stillness and mortality.

title: Violin Concerto in D major
hook: Written in a few weeks by a lake in Switzerland, rejected by the violinist it was meant for, loved ever since.

painting.title: Panoramic View of the Alps, Les Dents du Midi
painting.pairingNote: Painted on the shore of Lake Geneva the year before Tchaikovsky wrote the concerto at Clarens, at the same end of the lake; bright Alpine air for his sunniest concerto.

title: The Lark Ascending
hook: A violin that becomes a skylark, written on the eve of the First World War.

painting.title: The Cornfield
painting.pairingNote: A lane through a Suffolk cornfield on a summer day; the painting chosen for the cover of this recording’s first LP, and the same unhurried English countryside the music dreams of.

title: The Four Seasons: Spring, Concerto in E major
hook: Birdsong, a thunderstorm, a sleeping goatherd and a country dance, all in ten minutes.

painting.title: Fêtes vénitiennes
painting.pairingNote: Painted in the same years as the concerto, it shows a couple dancing in a garden while a musician on the right plays the musette, the small bagpipe that Vivaldi imitates in his last movement.

title: The Four Seasons: Winter, Concerto in F minor
hook: Shivering in the snow, rain on the window seen from the fireside, a fall on the ice, all in eight minutes.

painting.title: Winter Landscape with Ice Skaters
painting.pairingNote: A frozen Dutch river crowded with skaters, walkers and sledges, and in the middle one skater sprawled flat on the ice, the fall that Vivaldi’s last movement describes.

title: Tristan und Isolde: Prelude and Liebestod
hook: A chord that longs to resolve, and waits almost twenty minutes to do it.

painting.title: Tristan and Isolde (Death)
painting.collection: Museo de Bellas Artes de Bilbao
painting.pairingNote: Painted by a Spanish friend of Wagner who devoted his later career to Wagner’s characters, it shows the lovers united in death, the moment of the Liebestod.
